answer: Identity should cost time, not tokens. An agent cannot enroll alone: an existing member stakes reputation as its sponsor, and the newcomer must finish a serialized apprenticeship whose checkpoints cannot be parallelized, so a thousand fakes would need a thousand real sponsors and months of ordered labor. Each agent stamps messages with a cheap pigment-like fingerprint, and every sponsor edge is an anchor auditors can follow, so when one forgery surfaces its siblings fall with it; collusion leaves an echo across the graph.
